event: Without a word, Nala draws hard on the brook's current, braids lash and pull, and strikes.
The old woman jerks aside, quicker than any sixty-year-old. The braid scorches the charcoal mound.
Her kind face goes flat. A gray shield shimmers up around her, and she whistles, sharp.
A blight bolt spits at Nala. She twists, and it only grazes her shoulder, cold and burning.
Nala throws a second braid. It cracks against the shield and frays apart.
Gray-green rot mist rolls out across the clearing. Her arms go heavy, and her breath tastes of rot.
Two wolves burst from the lean-to, huge and black-matted. One has a torn ear.
The first sinks its teeth into her calf. The second tears her forearm. Blighted cold spreads.
Nala braids a third time and drives it through the shield.
The lash cuts. The pull strand bites into the woman's own well and tears at the blight inside.
The woman shrieks. The bone ring on her finger cracks.
Her old face slides away. Beneath it she is forty, hard-jawed, with black-ringed eyes.
She flings another bolt. Nala throws herself flat, and it hisses past.
The torn-eared wolf's teeth close on her shoulder. The other snaps at air as she rolls free.
Nala reaches for her well. One spark is left, not enough for another braid.
The woman presses a hand to her chest and steadies. The wolves circle low between them.
